principles: Execute the approved root cleanup rather than producing another explanation document.
Preserve user-owned and entrypoint root files exactly unless the cleanup requires reference updates elsewhere.
Archive historical legacy material instead of rewriting policy claims during cleanup.
Keep host-neutral Lattice boundaries and avoid new capability or production-safety claims.
drivers: The user explicitly asked to remove root directory document pollution.
The final allowed root set is already decided by the migration solution.
The root files are large legacy docs, so full semantic merge in one cleanup story would be risky and unnecessary.
Reference scans must not leave ordinary docs pointing at removed root paths.

options.name: A: Archive legacy root Markdown and update references
pros: Immediately cleans the repository root to the approved allowed set.
Preserves historical content for audit without keeping root stubs.
Avoids risky bulk rewriting of established truth-source docs.
cons: Some archived documents remain historical rather than active canonical truth sources.

options.name: B: Fully merge every legacy root document into active decision docs before deleting
pros: Could reduce reliance on archive references later.
cons: Large semantic rewrite in one story would be high risk.
It could accidentally introduce or duplicate capability and Production Safety claims.
It goes beyond the user-visible cleanup target.

options.name: C: Delete non-allowed root files without preserving them
cons: Risky loss of historical context and harder audit trail.
Reference updates would be harder to justify where historical lineage is still mentioned.

chosen: A: Archive legacy root Markdown and update references
rationale: Choose archival cleanup because it directly satisfies the user-visible root inventory goal while preserving historical context and avoiding arbitrary semantic rewrites or new capability claims.

preMortem.scenario: The cleanup deletes jek.md or allowed root entrypoints by accident.
preMortem.trigger: Bulk find/delete command operates on all root Markdown files instead of the explicit denylist.
preMortem.consequence: User-owned or entrypoint docs are damaged and the root contract is violated.
preMortem.mitigation: Use an explicit cleanup candidate list and verify the final inventory equals the five allowed files.

preMortem.scenario: Archived legacy docs continue to be referenced as active truth source.
preMortem.trigger: References are updated to archive files without clarifying historical context where needed.
preMortem.consequence: Readers may treat retired root docs as current policy.
preMortem.mitigation: Prefer active canonical decision docs for active references and reserve archive links for historical lineage only.

preMortem.scenario: The cleanup creates new overclaims while moving text.
preMortem.trigger: Agent tries to summarize Production Safety or capability content in active docs.
preMortem.consequence: The repo may imply readiness that has not been proven.
preMortem.mitigation: Avoid semantic merging in this story and run no-overclaim scans for Production Safety, capability, authority, and unattended wording.

preMortem.scenario: Reference scans remain noisy due intentional code compatibility references to KOALA.md.
preMortem.trigger: The scan treats all code/template mentions as broken root-doc references.
preMortem.consequence: The story churns compatibility code unnecessarily.
preMortem.mitigation: Separate documentation reader links from code compatibility/test mentions; document intentional code mentions as legacy asset compatibility, not root file retention.
